source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter III, §18 Attacking with Knights as a Prominent Force, Example 46

steps.title: Press on
steps.source: White is two Pawns behind. He must therefore press on his attack.

narration.say: Now the knights play a prominent part.
White is two pawns behind, so he must press on with his attack. Both knights are near the black king.

feedback.Nhxg7: The other knight: the one on f5 takes g7.
feedback.*: A knight takes the pawn on g7.

exercise.prompt: White to move. A knight takes a pawn.
exercise.hint: The f5 knight takes on g7.

steps.title: Your turn: take the rook
steps.source: Evidently an error which made the winning easier for White, as he simply took the Rook with the Knight and kept up the attack.

narration.say: An error, which made things easier for White.

feedback.*: The knight on g7 can take a rook.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Win the exchange and keep the attack.
exercise.wrong: The knight on g7 can take a rook.
exercise.success: 2. Nxe8, and White kept up the attack.

narration.say: Black should have taken the knight.
Knight to f6, check. King to g6.
Knight takes the bishop, and f6 is best.
Pawn to e5. King to f7.
Knight takes f6, rook to e7. Knight to e4, and Black should lose.
